ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma to the lung
Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma to the bone

facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm
A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm

concepts.why: The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and the current presentation of a subcutaneous mass and multiple nodules in the liver and lungs is consistent with metastatic disease.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of a primary soft tissue sarcoma.

concepts.preferred_label: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma to the lung
concepts.why: The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules in a patient with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma is consistent with lung metastasis.

concepts.preferred_label: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma to the bone
concepts.why: The presence of a subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib in a patient with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma is consistent with bone metastasis.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of an undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of a dedifferentiated liposarcoma.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of a leiomyosarcoma.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of an Ewing sarcoma.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass with aggressive features and the uncertainty of the primary site of the tumor raise the possibility of an osteosarcoma.

rationales.F01: The presence of a subcutaneous nodule is more typical of extrahepatic metastasis of HCC or a primary soft tissue sarcoma.
rationales.F06: The subcutaneous mass is consistent with either a primary soft tissue sarcoma or an extrahepatic metastasis of HCC.
rationales.F10: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels are strongly associated with HCC.
rationales.F11: The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules is consistent with metastatic disease, including HCC.
rationales.F12: The abdominal CT findings of multiple nodules in the liver and a right-flank soft tissue mass are highly suggestive of extrahepatic metastasis of HCC.
